stem: On the chest radiograph in Case 5, the consolidation is located in which lobe?

options.text: Basal segment of right upper lobe

explanation: The most likely location of the consolidation is the right middle lobe, based on the lobar silhouette pattern described in the case. The question is asking you to localise the opacity using chest X-ray anatomy rather than identify the organism or diagnosis.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Chest X-Ray - Part B

rationale: The source item does not include the radiograph itself or a marked correct option, so it is safest to rewrite it into a clear single-best-answer question while preserving the clinical concept of lobar localisation on chest X-ray.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: right middle lobe consolidation commonly silhouettes the right heart border.
optionExplanations.B: Would more typically affect the right hemidiaphragm rather than the right heart border.
optionExplanations.C: This is part of the right upper lobe, but not the typical location suggested here.
optionExplanations.D: Included as a distractor; left-sided disease would not fit the described right-sided lobar anatomy.

Instructions

Questions 13 -17 relate to Case 5

Case 5

Various structures are visible on the chest radiograph because of the density difference between them and the anatomically adjacent aerated lung. The replacement of alveolar air by soft tissue density, such as secretions, inflammatory fluid or oedema, will remove the density gradient and the borders will no longer be distinguishable, known as the silhouette sign.

It is important to understand the lobar anatomy and thus the location of infection when interpreting the radiograph. The following five questions will help you practise this skill.
